credentials.description: client_id of the environment (sandbox: developer account dashboard; production: Settings → API Keys, v4)

example_prompt: Fetch the chargebacks raised against my Flutterwave account so I can respond before they are lost.

page.description: Query parameter. The page of the data to retrieve. The most recent data entry is on page 1.

size.description: Query parameter. Length of data returned. Defaults to 10.

from.description: Query parameter. The start date and time for a period. This parameter is used in conjunction with the 'to' parameter to define a time range. The value should be in ISO 8601 format.

to.description: Query parameter. The end date and time for a period. This parameter is used in conjunction with the 'from' parameter to define a time range. The value should be in **ISO 8601 format**.

total.description: The total number of items available across all pages

current_page.description: The current page number being viewed

total_pages.description: The total number of pages required to display all items.

charge_id.description: ID of the charge tied to this chargeback

stage.description: The stage describes the current phase of a chargeback dispute

status.description: The status field tracks the current state or outcome of a chargeback dispute, providing a comprehensive overview of its lifecycle.

type.description: The type categorizes the chargeback based on whether it originates from a transaction within the same country (local) or across different countries (international).

due_datetime.description: The due_datetime specifies the exact date and time by which an action or response is required. This is typically used to set deadlines for submitting documentation or responding to a chargeback.

created_datetime.description: The created_datetime indicates the exact date and time when the chargeback record was initially created in the system. This timestamp helps in tracking the age of the dispute.

updated_datetime.description: The updated_datetime specifies the most recent date and time when any information related to the chargeback record was modified or updated. This helps in tracking the last activity on the dispute.

settlement_id.description: ID of the settlement tied to this chargeback

message.description: Present on 401/403/409 bodies; the 400 body has none.

type.description: Error category. Generic: REQUEST_NOT_VALID, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; or a domain type (see code).

code.description: String. Generic 10400/10401/10403/10404/10409/10422/10500, or a domain code documented for this endpoint: 1700404 CHARGEBACK_NOT_FOUND.

gotchas: Auth: one token server for both environments — the docs' Multi-Environment Integrations example sends either environment's credentials to https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, and Authentication says "This process applies to both the sandbox and production environments. Make sure to use the correct credentials for each environment to obtain a valid token." "Each token is valid for **10 minutes**"; "We recommend refreshing the token at least one minute before it expires." Cache the token. Sandbox: "We archive your test data after 30 days."

Headers: X-Trace-Id is optional on this GET (the headers guide lists it under 'Optional API Headers'; "It must be a string using only alphanumeric ASCII characters.", 12-255 characters). The API reference documents no X-Idempotency-Key for this endpoint.

Discovery: Docs (Chargebacks): "Flutterwave notifies you about chargebacks via your email." "We also send webhooks to your server when a chargeback is raised. This notification service is available on request." Without the webhook, poll this endpoint at least hourly (from = last poll): the guide's samples set due_datetime 24 hours after created_datetime.
Respond before data.due_datetime: lost means "a lack of response from the merchant before the due date (48 hours)"; "If the merchant **does not respond**, the amount is debited automatically."

Status: accepted / declined = you answered; won / lost / reversed = final; anything else (initiated, pending, and new, which the API enum has but the guide's table doesn't describe) = waiting for you. Stage pre-arbitration = last chance to send new evidence.

Pagination: page ≥ 1 (default 1, most recent first), size 10-50 (default 10); read meta.page_info.total_pages. The API reference caps some list responses at 10 items (maxItems 10) although size goes up to 50: always paginate.

Errors: {"status":"failed","error":{"type","code","message","validation_errors"}}; error.code is a string and 400s carry validation_errors[{field_name,message}]. Besides the generic codes (10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID, 10401, 10403 FORBIDDEN, 10404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 10409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, 10422 UNPROCESSABLE, 10500) the error table documents these for this endpoint: 1700404 CHARGEBACK_NOT_FOUND. Branch on error.type / error.code, not on the HTTP status alone. Docs (Errors): "The current limit is 500 API requests per minute." A 429 can come back as a non-JSON page ("HTML error pages such as `Cloudflare 1015 responses`"): parse error bodies defensively and back off exponentially with jitter.
open_questions: Token URL: the PHP sample of Authentication uses https://keycloak.dev-flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token; its curl and JavaScript samples and the Multi-Environment example use https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, which this spec follows.
